data.name: Tesnovar Wardenry
data.short_lore: Tesnovan forest villages have never bowed to a crown: each elects its Warden from among its hunters, and the Oath of Lisnik Gate binds them. Their longbowmen ambush the roads near Hrastovec and Ukrenvar, and the Regency's tax-men are their favourite prey. The Fen clans claim the marsh-edge timber of Smrekovo, and that quarrel is turning cold oaths hot.

towns.name: Brezhnik
towns.blurb: Birch-bark tanners' market; every Warden's election is held under its great oak council tree.

towns.name: Ostrogrado
towns.blurb: Walled market-town where the Compact's oath-rolls are kept and feuds are settled by the bowstring.

towns.name: Mirkovice
towns.blurb: Honey and wax trading town, with a lingering grudge over a beehive tax the Regency tried to levy.

towns.name: Lipnevo
towns.blurb: Linden-wood carvers and bowyers; its yew-stave workshops supply half the Compact's longbows.

towns.name: Sosnograd
towns.blurb: Pine-timber river port where log rafts float down to the Fen's reed markets.

towns.name: Dolivar
towns.blurb: Valley town famous for its bell-founders, whose bells warn of raiders across the hills.

castles.name: Vodnagrad
castles.blurb: Lake fortress that refused the king's tax-collectors for three generations.

castles.name: Hrastovec
castles.blurb: Oak-ringed hillfort where the first Warden was chosen by a hunter's arrow.

castles.name: Ukrenvar
castles.blurb: Stone keep built by the Regency and now a Compact prize, held by a disputed garrison.

castles.name: Ruzhovec
castles.blurb: Rose-thorn hedge fort whose ditches are said to have been dug by the forest's own spirits.

castles.name: Yasenvar
castles.blurb: Ash-tree castle with a legend that its gate opens only for a Warden's true heir.

castles.name: Stribogra
castles.blurb: Wind-watch tower on the ridge; its keepers light beacons to warn the villages below.

castles.name: Vezhdrak
castles.blurb: Crumbling watchtower whose broken stair is a favourite ambush spot for outlaws.

castles.name: Chernoyar
castles.blurb: Black-stone bluff fort, a grudge site where villagers hanged a king's marshal from its gate.

castles.name: Pelnik
castles.blurb: Moss-walled ruin where the Compact's first oath was broken, and the stones still remember.

villages.name: Hlivno
villages.blurb: Mud-brick village famous for its clay ovens and the bread that feeds the Wardens' hunts.

villages.name: Brusnice
villages.blurb: Berry-picking hamlet where the pickers swear their oaths over cups of sour cider.

villages.name: Dubnyak
villages.blurb: Oak-cutters' village with a long feud against the Salt-road's timber caravans.

villages.name: Zhelnice
villages.blurb: Ironwood gatherers; a legend says the first bow of the Compact was carved here.

villages.name: Oshnivo
villages.blurb: Hunters' lodge village known for its hounds; a famous bear once killed a Regency marshal.

villages.name: Kravnik
villages.blurb: Cattle-breeders on the fen edge who still pay a yearly toll to the reed clans.

villages.name: Tranok
villages.blurb: Charcoal-burners' hamlet; the black smoke draws unwelcome riders in the dry season.

villages.name: Mokrenka
villages.blurb: Damp village built on stilts, with a grudge over a Warden who drowned in its millpond.

villages.name: Volchyk
villages.blurb: Wolf-trapper village whose pelts are prized in the River-guild cities, which overcharge them.

villages.name: Smrekovo
villages.blurb: Spruce-resin village at the marsh edge, site of the disputed timber line with the Fen.

villages.name: Redlice
villages.blurb: Red-clay pottery village whose kilns scent the air for miles on festival nights.

villages.name: Gorvenka
villages.blurb: Mountain-pass hamlet where herdsmen once stopped an Ashland priest's procession.

villages.name: Sedlov
villages.blurb: Saddle-makers' village that sells fine horse gear to whichever lord pays best.

villages.name: Bukhrov
villages.blurb: Beech-wood hamlet with a shrine to the Hunter's Oath, carved into a living tree.

villages.name: Lyutoda
villages.blurb: Stone-bridge village where the river toll is collected by the Warden's sworn men.

villages.name: Chorvena
villages.blurb: Forest chapel village whose bell is rung backward when a Warden is slain.

villages.name: Vrasnik
villages.blurb: Crow-watch village whose scouts are trained to read the birds' warnings from the canopy.

villages.name: Pesnitsa
villages.blurb: Singers' village where the Compact's oath-songs were first written down by a monk.

villages.name: Radomesh
villages.blurb: Quiet farm village in a forest clearing, famous for its beekeepers' hard cheese.

villages.name: Jelovec
villages.blurb: Fir-wood logging camp, sworn to the Warden and hostile to the Salt-road's wagons.

villages.name: Sukovrat
villages.blurb: Dry-hill village with a grudge against the southern mining towns over poisoned wells.
